concerns.text: FR-003 mandates an ablation study across 'at least three distinct model variants'. The tasks (T026a) only define two specific variants ('no_recurrence', 'no_inhibition') plus the 'full' model. A third distinct variant (e.g., 'no_homeostasis' or 'altered_topology') is missing from the task list, leaving the requirement unfulfillable.

SC-002 requires measuring 'training stability' against a baseline gradient norm distribution to verify homeostatic scaling efficacy. Tasks T008b and T019 only specify logging gradient norms to a JSON file. There is no task to compute the distributional comparison or verify the efficacy, leaving the success criterion unmeasurable.

FR-008 requires scaling law analysis. Task T050 extends this to an 8x column variant to satisfy a reviewer request, but there is no task to validate that the 8x variant fits within the 6-hour CPU time limit (FR-004) before execution. This risks a failed CI run or scope violation without a mitigation task.

Tasks T060–T064 implement a 'Rule Space Search' to address Stephen Wolfram's feedback. This capability is not authorized by spec.md (which defines scope as implementing a parameterized microcircuit and running ablation/scaling studies). This constitutes unapproved scope creep that risks violating the 6-hour CPU constraint.

Task T011b requires implementing a Kolmogorov-Smirnov test to verify statistical independence between training and test sets. spec.md User Story 1 only requires using an independent test set (Lorenz vs. Polynomials) and verifying a degradation metric. The task introduces a specific statistical verification method not defined in the spec's acceptance criteria.
